articles.title: Home Assistant repairs updates blocked by GitHub downloads
articles.dek: Core 2026.10.4 includes the firmware-download correction; related fixes cover OS and Marketplace downloads.
body: Home Assistant repairs downloads rejected after GitHub began sending larger security headers with its release files. The failure can block Home Assistant OS updates, hardware firmware updates and repository downloads in the new Marketplace before the file itself arrives.

Core 2026.10.4, published on October 24, includes the shared-client correction used by hardware firmware downloads. The Supervisor and Marketplace fixes address the same failure separately; they are not part of that Core patch. The connections accept larger response headers instead of rejecting GitHub’s roughly 9 KiB header at the previous limit of about 8 KiB.

Raise header size limits of the Supervisor websession

articles.title: Music Assistant makes WLED lights react to music
articles.dek: Lighting zones follow a grouped speaker through WLED’s native audio-sync connection.
body: Music Assistant adds a connection that makes WLED lights react to the music playing through a speaker. Will Tatam makes his first contribution to Music Assistant’s server with the addition. Each connection represents a lighting zone, and grouping its virtual player with a real speaker supplies the audio information that drives the lights.

A zone is identified by a network port rather than one light’s address. WLED devices join it by selecting the matching audio-sync port in their own settings, allowing several lights to follow the same zone. The connection carries loudness, frequency and rhythm information through WLED’s existing audio-sync protocol.

articles.title: ESPHome updates Adafruit Nordic boards over Bluetooth
articles.dek: Wireless uploads reach boards using the Adafruit bootloader, with recovery available to previously paired hosts.
body: ESPHome adds Bluetooth firmware uploads for nRF52 boards using the Adafruit bootloader, including nice!nano, ItsyBitsy and Feather nRF52840. Ömer Şiar Baysal makes his first contribution to ESPHome with the addition, extending the command-line uploader beyond its existing MCUboot route.

The Bluetooth service also starts in safe mode, allowing a previously paired computer to recover a board stuck restarting. Safe mode rejects new pairings because it does not run the automation that approves them. Normal operation should enable pairing to restrict who can request an update.

Hardware checks covered a nice!nano and an ItsyBitsy, including an upload from macOS. A board still running the old update service needs one update through its existing method before the new route works.

articles.title: Home Assistant explains what to do when backups fail
articles.dek: New troubleshooting guidance separates failing storage, blocked restores and damaged backup files.
body: Home Assistant’s backup guide adds practical recovery steps for storage errors, restores that refuse to start and backups that cannot be read. For failing local storage, it puts copying a backup and saving its encryption key ahead of replacing the device.

The guide explains why a restore can temporarily leave the ordinary interface showing “Not found” and how Home Assistant OS owners can follow Supervisor’s progress through the Observer. It also distinguishes an incomplete archive from a wrong encryption key, while noting that a damaged encrypted backup can produce the same error as a wrong key.

The guide also spells out the internet, system-health and free-space checks that can prevent a restore from starting. It advises leaving an active restore running rather than switching the system off when the ordinary interface disappears.

articles.title: ESPHome shares a cellular connection through a Wi-Fi hotspot
articles.dek: Other Wi-Fi devices can use the modem connection, while a setup portal remains reachable during an upstream outage.
body: ESPHome extends its new cellular modem connection into a Wi-Fi hotspot: devices joining the ESP32’s access point can route internet traffic through the modem. Yesterday’s component supplied connectivity to the ESPHome device itself; this addition shares that connection with other devices.

Companion access-point work keeps a setup portal available while the upstream connection is down and closes the portal when the station reconnects, without closing the access point. A separate always-on mode keeps an access point beside the home-network connection without routing traffic.

articles.title: Music Assistant restores Nicovideo playback and changes sign-in
articles.dek: An upstream change requires a saved session cookie instead of an email address and password.
body: Music Assistant restores track details and playback for Nico Nico Video after the service changed its responses on October 21. The same update removes email-and-password sign-in, which the service’s new verification requirement and retired login endpoint had already made unusable.

Existing installations keep using the session saved at their last successful sign-in. When it expires, the owner must enter a fresh user_session cookie in the provider’s settings; automatic password-based renewal is gone. The settings migration deletes the previously stored email address, password and verification values. 柴田 makes a first contribution to Music Assistant’s documentation with the matching setup guide.

pullRequests.title: Fix Nicovideo playback and track details after the watch API change
Nico Nico Video: user_session cookie is now the only login method

articles.title: ESPHome keeps working while web requests wait
articles.dek: Measured pauses shrink on ESP32 devices, with a change needed for scripts that repeat requests.
body: ESPHome reduces the time that web requests hold up the rest of a device’s work. On ESP32 devices using recent ESP-IDF builds, requests proceed in steps while other work runs; the actions after a request still wait for its response.

On a T-Display S3 Pro with ESP-IDF 5.5.6, an ordinary HTTPS request’s worst main-loop pause fell from roughly 2.4–2.5 seconds to 0.30–0.36 seconds across two runs. Total request time stayed about the same. Some connection and encryption work still pauses the device, and an unreachable host can block for the full timeout.

A script containing a request remains running until the response arrives. Scripts using the default single-run mode skip another trigger during that time; makers who need every trigger must choose queued or parallel mode. Arduino and host builds retain the previous blocking request behaviour.

pullRequests.title: [http_request] Run requests from the action without blocking the loop

articles.title: Home Assistant reads Helty temperatures and filter condition
articles.dek: Cloud-connected ventilation units report humidity, treated air and their own filter alarm.
body: Home Assistant adds indoor and outdoor temperature, indoor humidity and filter readings for Helty Flow Cloud ventilation units. The filter problem sensor follows the unit’s own alarm, while another reading measures the volume of air treated since the last filter change.

Ermanno Baschiera extends the fan controls introduced earlier this week. These readings reuse the existing cloud updates without extra requests. They do not add the optional carbon-dioxide or air-quality probes, which need separate checks for whether the sensors are fitted.

pullRequests.title: Add sensor platform to Helty Flow Cloud
Add filter alarm binary sensor to Helty Flow Cloud

articles.title: Home Assistant adds controls for Tesla’s solar charging
articles.dek: An opt-in preview changes charge-on-solar settings, with requested values retained because the vehicle cannot report them back.
body: Home Assistant’s Teslemetry connection adds an opt-in Labs preview for switching a compatible vehicle’s charge-on-solar mode on or off and setting its lower charging limit. The upper limit uses the vehicle’s existing charge-limit control.

The new controls keep an assumed state because the API cannot read back the feature’s live settings. Their last requested values are stored together so disabling one entity does not leave the other sending an outdated limit. The vehicle needs the required account permission.

pullRequests.title: Add Labs charge-on-solar switch and lower limit to Teslemetry
Add Labs charge-on-solar switch and lower limit to Teslemetry

articles.title: ESPHome adjusts Delta wallbox charging current
articles.dek: A variable current limit gives automations more control than starting and stopping a session.
body: ESPHome adds an adjustable maximum current to its Delta AC wallbox connection. An automation can vary that limit for a solar-charging or household load-management setup rather than only start or stop charging.

The addition builds on yesterday’s Bluetooth controls and corrects the power, energy and elapsed-time readings. It supplies the current control; the decision about how much power to allocate still belongs to the maker’s automation.

pullRequests.title: [delta_wallbox] Added ability to set the max current

articles.title: ESPHome keeps climate controls on the right temperature scale
articles.dek: Explicit units convert correctly for Fahrenheit devices, while template heaters gain a choice of units.
body: ESPHome corrects temperature settings sent to Fahrenheit-based climate devices. A setting written as 30°C is converted to 86°F rather than being sent as 30°F to Friedrich, Islandaire or a Mitsubishi CN105 configured for Fahrenheit.

Template climate devices and water heaters also gain Celsius, Fahrenheit or Kelvin selection, matching the values supplied by their sensors and templates. Values written without a unit keep using the device’s own scale; other existing platforms retain Celsius.

pullRequests.title: [climate][water_heater] Add unit_of_measurement to the template climate and water heater

articles.title: Home Assistant finds the right Somfy region at sign-in
articles.dek: A unified setup offers a gateway picker for accounts with more than one hub.
body: Home Assistant adds a Somfy setup option that chooses the right region and server from the account instead of asking the owner to select a regional service. Accounts with several gateways receive a list of the hubs to connect.

Mick Vleeshouwer adds the option to Overkiz alongside its existing regional choices. It supports signing in again and changing the connection’s settings. Existing regional connections are unchanged; their migration remains separate work.

pullRequests.title: Add Somfy multi-account (email/password) config flow to Overkiz

articles.title: ESPHome keeps each device’s online status separate
articles.dek: Boards sharing one configuration gain distinct MQTT status messages, with delivery checked before shutdown.
body: ESPHome separates the online status of MQTT-connected boards built from the same configuration. When a device’s name includes its hardware-address suffix, that suffix also identifies its default status and log messages; previously the boards shared those messages despite having distinct names.

A companion change waits briefly for the message broker to acknowledge a shutdown message before disconnecting. Tests on ESP32 and ESP8266 boards received the message on every tested restart, where the old code missed most of them. The wait remains bounded by the shutdown timeout.
Custom topics remain unchanged. After updating a setup that uses name suffixes, the old shared status topic retains its last offline message and may need clearing if anything still watches it.

pullRequests.title: [mqtt] mqtt_client does not honor name_add_mac_suffix for default log_topic, birth_message, will_message, shutdown_message
[mqtt][core] Wait for the broker to confirm the shutdown message before disconnecting

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps mixed Raumfeld speaker groups playing
articles.dek: The stream follows the formats every room supports, rather than only the leading speaker.
body: Music Assistant chooses an audio format supported by every room in a Raumfeld group. Previously, a Stereo M limited to 96 kHz could fall silent after joining a One S playing at 192 kHz, because the host forwarded the stream without converting it for the less capable speaker.

When another room joins, the connection can restart the queue near its current position in a compatible format. Live radio restarts at the live point. Removing a room leaves the music playing at its existing format until the next start, and grouping rooms in the Raumfeld app follows the same check.

The check considers every format offered when playback started, so enabling higher sample rates can cause a restart even when the actual track did not need one. Simanias tested the change with a One S and Stereo M.

pullRequests.title: Play a Raumfeld group at a sample rate each of its rooms plays
Let the sample rates of each Raumfeld room be chosen, up to 96 kHz by default

articles.title: Home Assistant changes SteamVR base-station modes and channels
articles.dek: New controls join a fault reading received from the station’s Bluetooth broadcasts.
body: Home Assistant adds power-mode and channel controls for compatible SteamVR base stations. The power selector offers On, Sleep and Standby, giving automations a direct way to choose the station’s operating mode.
A separate problem sensor reports a fault received passively in the station’s Bluetooth broadcasts.

articles.title: Home Assistant moves AlarmDecoder without rebuilding its zones
articles.dek: Changing the connection preserves the alarm’s zone definitions and arming settings.
body: Home Assistant adds a reconfiguration flow for AlarmDecoder connections, so changing an IP address, port or serial connection no longer requires deleting the integration and rebuilding every zone. The new connection is checked before it is saved, while existing zone definitions and arming settings remain intact.
Paul Traina adds the flow. A name chosen by the owner stays unchanged, and selecting a device already used by another connection is rejected.

articles.title: Home Assistant connects Advantage Air tablets without remote registration
articles.dek: Locally used tablets can identify themselves without a cloud-issued identifier.
body: Home Assistant repairs setup for Advantage Air tablets that have never registered for remote access, such as a Zone10e used on a network without internet. Those tablets can omit the identifier previously required by the setup flow, causing it to fail.

The connection uses the tablet’s alternative identifier when the remote-access identifier is absent. Existing installations keep their identities; a tablet supplying neither receives a clear setup error.

articles.title: Home Assistant reads the fill level of BleBox tanks
articles.dek: Tank sensors supply liquid height, volume and pressure, with guidance for an unconfigured probe.
body: Home Assistant adds fill percentage, liquid height, volume and pressure readings from BleBox tankSensor devices. The measurements bring the tank’s reported contents into dashboards and automations.

If the device reports that its probe is not configured, Home Assistant raises a repair directing the owner to configure it in the wBox app. The repair clears automatically when the probe starts supplying readings.

articles.title: Home Assistant shows Blink’s arm state without a five-minute wait
articles.dek: Alarm and motion controls update after successful commands instead of waiting for the next poll.
body: Home Assistant stops leaving Blink alarm controls showing their previous state for up to five minutes after an arm or disarm command. The connection reads the alarm module’s state immediately; a camera’s motion switch records a successful command and lets the next poll correct it if necessary.

In the contributor’s test on Home Assistant 2026.10.2 with one sync module, arm, disarm and motion-switch changes appeared within about 0.2 to 0.3 seconds with this correction and a companion refresh-rate change. Previously, the tested arm command took five minutes to appear.

pullRequests.title: Show the new Blink arm state right after a command
